stem: A retail collaborative agreement purports to let the pharmacist prescribe alprazolam and methylphenidate. Select all supported conclusions.

choices.text: The agreement cannot authorize retail pharmacist prescribing of Schedule II through V substances.
Professional liability insurance waives the schedule restriction.
The controlled-substance limitation applies even if the supervising physician signs the agreement.
Only Schedule II is prohibited; Schedule IV is allowed.
A verbal patient consent converts the drugs to Schedule VI.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. A retail collaborative practice agreement may not authorize the pharmacist to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances.

choice_analysis.A: The proposition 'The agreement cannot authorize retail pharmacist prescribing of Schedule II through V substances.' is supported by Retail CDTM Schedule II through V prohibition: A retail collaborative practice agreement may not authorize the pharmacist to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances.
choice_analysis.B: This statement imports Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.C: The proposition 'The controlled-substance limitation applies even if the supervising physician signs the agreement.' is supported by Retail CDTM Schedule II through V prohibition: A retail collaborative practice agreement may not authorize the pharmacist to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances.
choice_analysis.D: This statement imports Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This statement imports Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.

related_facts: A retail collaborative practice agreement may not authorize the pharmacist to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances.
explanation.mpje_trap: Selecting a familiar statement without checking whether its schedule, setting, deadline, and exception match the facts.
